skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automates Twitter/X workflows through the inference.sh belt CLI, including posts, media posts, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, deletes, and profile lookups.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh belt commands for Twitter/X posting, engagement, messages, follows, and profile lookups.
skill.author: inference-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown formatting around examples, not embedded Ruby execution. The skill still grants broad belt CLI access and documents write actions against a Twitter/X account, including posts, DMs, follows, retweets, and deletes. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the specific x/* app commands required by this skill, or require explicit user confirmation for every belt command.
Add clear approval, rate limit, recipient validation, and policy checks before posting, messaging, following, liking, retweeting, or deleting.
Pin related skill and CLI installation instructions to reviewed versions instead of branch-based or unverified sources.

semantic_findings.title: Broad External CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash access to belt with a wildcard pattern and later encourages browsing all apps. This allows more inference.sh operations than the documented Twitter/X app set.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools front matter explicitly permits Bash(belt *), and the document references all apps with belt app list. The risk is broad tool scope, not inferred hidden behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Twitter/X Account Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents posting, liking, retweeting, deleting, direct messaging, and following from an authenticated account. These write actions can cause spam, account misuse, or unwanted public changes without approvals.

content.value_statement: Twitter/X posting and engagement can require repeated API calls and careful input formatting. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code command patterns for inference.sh belt apps.
actual_capabilities: Shows belt commands for posting text tweets with x/post-tweet.
Shows media post workflows with x/post-create and an input file.
Provides examples for liking, retweeting, deleting, and fetching posts.
Provides examples for sending direct messages and following users.
Demonstrates image and video generation workflows before posting media URLs.
Links to inference.sh documentation for X integration and app usage.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Does not add rate limits, moderation checks, or approval workflows.
Examples use placeholder IDs, usernames, and media URLs.
Depends on inference.sh, X permissions, and external service availability.

use_cases.title: Publish Approved Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and post approved product updates or announcements with consistent belt command inputs.

use_cases.title: Share Developer Releases
use_cases.description: Post release notes, generated images, or demo videos to an authenticated Twitter/X account.

use_cases.title: Check Public Profiles
use_cases.description: Fetch post or user details by ID or username before planning outreach or support responses.

prompt_templates.title: Post Approved Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to post this approved text to Twitter/X: [text]. Show the command and ask for confirmation before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to prepare a media post with this message and media URL: [message], [media URL]. Validate the inputs first.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to like or retweet this post ID: [post ID]. Confirm the account and action before any write operation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Generated Media Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to generate media with inference.sh, prepare the Twitter/X post, and list every external action before execution.

output_examples.input: Post the approved launch message to Twitter/X.
output_examples.output: Prepared a text post action for the authenticated account. The final message is ready for review before posting.

output_examples.input: Create a post using this product image URL.
output_examples.output: Prepared a media post workflow with the provided image URL and a short caption. The post should be approved before execution.

output_examples.input: Look up this public profile before outreach.
output_examples.output: Prepared a profile lookup action using the supplied username. No write action is needed for this request.

best_practices: Confirm the account, text, recipient, and action before every write operation.
Respect X platform rules, consent requirements, and internal approval policies.
Verify media ownership, content accuracy, and destination URLs before posting.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk likes, follows, retweets, or direct messages without review.
Do not post generated media without checking rights, accuracy, and disclosure needs.
Do not install related skills or CLI tools from mutable sources without review.

faq.question: Does this skill post directly to Twitter/X?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI commands that can post through inference.sh when the account is authenticated and permissions allow it.

faq.question: Can it send direct messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a direct message example that needs a recipient ID and approved message text.

faq.question: Does it include safeguards against spam?
faq.answer: No. Users must add approval checks, rate limits, and policy controls before automated engagement.

faq.question: Can it post images or videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows media post examples and workflows that use generated image or video URLs.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The inference.sh belt CLI must be installed and logged in to an account with the required X integration permissions.

faq.question: Is it limited to read-only actions?
faq.answer: No. It includes write actions such as posting, deleting, liking, retweeting, messaging, and following.
